lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS’ OFFICE - DAY
lines.dialogue: How do you mean?

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS’ OFFICE - DAY
lines.dialogue: You vouched for him previously. I took you at your word.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS’ OFFICE - DAY
lines.dialogue: I’m told his product was more or less consistent with the quality I had come to expect.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS’ OFFICE - DAY
lines.dialogue: But it doesn’t.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS’ OFFICE - DAY
lines.dialogue: I apologize for being so transparent.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS’ OFFICE - DAY
lines.dialogue: Would you take a drive with me? I’d like to show you something.
Please.
Your new lab.
I had excellent help. As will you. Quite a lot of planning went into this.

The laundry upstairs, I’ve owned it for years. It receives large chemical deliveries on a weekly basis -- detergents and such. There’s nothing suspicious about it. And my employees, to be sure, are well-trained. Trustworthy. The filtration system is state-of- the-art. It will vent nothing but clean, odorless steam. Just as the laundry does, and through the very same stacks.
I need two hundred pounds per week to make this economically viable.
You would choose your own hours, of course, come and go as you please. So long as the quota is met.
Why did you make these decisions?
Then they weren’t bad decisions. What does a man do, Walter? A man provides for his family.

When you have children, you always have family. They will always be your priority. Your responsibility. And a man..? A man provides. And he does it even when he’s not appreciated... or respected... or even loved. He simply bears up, and he does it. Because he’s a man.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS FRING
lines.dialogue: So we try to clean them every night. But make sure it’s off before you open the intake valve...

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - GUS FRING
lines.dialogue: Good. Now, I suggest that you add this to your Monday maintenance schedule...

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - MORNING - MOMENTS LATER
lines.dialogue: Ah... morning.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - MORNING - MOMENTS LATER
lines.dialogue: Why? They’re doing nothing wrong.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - MORNING - MOMENTS LATER
lines.dialogue: Okay, let’s put this pepper here...
Cynthia, it’s okay. I’ll handle this.
What can I do for you?
Sunset.
I told you before. You will not kill Walter White. Not until my business with him has concluded.
You’ll have to. The decision isn’t yours to make.
Explain to me -- why this man White? He betrayed your cousin Tuco, yes... but he’s not the one who murdered him. Was there not another man who pulled the trigger?
North of the border is my territory. My say. As a show of respect, I say yes.
The agent’s name is Hank Schrader. May his death satisfy you.
Ah, Walter. You’re right on time. Please... come in.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I hope you like Paila Marina...

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: It’s a fancy name for fish stew. It sounds like a cliche, but indeed, it’s just like my mother used to make.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Come on. You can help me cook.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: This is a Chilean dish that I love, but... I never get to make it. Kids won’t eat it. But, uh... You know how that is.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Do you mind...?

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Wwould you slice the garlic? Very thin.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: We’re working together... why not break bread together?

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Now... the garlic?

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: It always amazes me... the way the senses work in connection to memory. This stew is simply an amalgam of ingredients. Taken separately, these ingredients alone don’t remind me of anything. Not very much at all. But in this precise combination? The smell of this meal..? Instantly, it brings me back to my childhood. How is that possible?

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: That’s very interesting.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Walter. I would like to help you, if I could.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Well, when I first started out, I made a lot of mistakes. More than I care to admit. I wish I’d had someone to advise me. Because this life of ours... it can overwhelm. You’re a wealthy man now. And one must learn to be rich. To be poor? Anyone can manage.

lines.scene: INT. SUBURBAN HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Never make the same mistake twice.
Has your condition worsened?
Your medical condition. Has it grown worse?
Is there a ringing in your ears? Are you seeing bright lights, or hearing voices?
No, clearly you’re not. No rational person would do as you have done. Explain yourself.
Some worthless junkie. For him you “intervene” and put us all at risk. Some contemptible junkie who couldn’t keep the peace for eight hours.
I heard about it. He should have let me take care of them.
Are you asking me if I ordered the murder of a child?
Where is Pinkman now?
What is Option B?
You’d need a new assistant.
No. This time I choose.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - OFFICE - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Where’d they cross?

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - OFFICE - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Probing for weakness.

lines.scene: INT. LOS POLLOS HERMANOS - OFFICE - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What about Pinkman?
Gale. It’s good to see you.
I should have called first. I’m not interrupting anything, am I?
Oh, no... no, thank you. I’m sorry for the inconvenience --
I need to talk to you about something. Something rather pressing.
If push came to shove, I was wondering how soon you might be able to take over the lab yourself. You, and, uh, an assistant.
Has Walter ever talked to you about why he got into this particular line of work..?
Oh, it is. But specifically, has he ever spoken to you about his health problems? I’m not surprised. He’s a very private person.
He’s dying of cancer.
It is why he does this. To provide for his family. Which he’s accomplished. They will never want for anything -- he’s seen to that.

That is very much the question. He does not want to talk about it. And every time I bring it up with him... I don’t know that he’s fully accepted the reality of it. And, not to sound cold-blooded... but I am running a business here.
I have a very large investment in this.
There’s so much overhead that I can’t afford to shut down. Not even for a week. So you understand my concern. And my desire for continuity.
Now, I intend to keep Walter on for as long as he wants, assuming he’s physically up to it. But as he cannot or will not tell me how long that might be... I must prepare for the worst-case scenario.
You don’t think you’re ready now?
I believe in you, Gale. I know that when the time comes, you will be ready.
